chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is
spiritual_reading:
When the good that engages directly with evil took into itself the outermost conditions of combat and held steady against the first uprising of opposition that had formed in falsity, it challenged the dominant evils that rule with persuasive power. These evils were beyond ordinary measure, surpassing what countless multiplied states can grasp. At first, when that good extended resistance against them, it let them receive the burning of their own distorted love and the volatility of their persuasive reasoning; and afterward it let the evil of spiritual death take on an external covering of truth in its lowest form. Then those ruling evils drew that truth into themselves and consumed it by turning it into falsity, as you have been told. From that external truth, once seized and perverted, many derivative falsities poured out in abundance, and streams of reasoning flowed on. The receptive craving of those ruling evils, and the powers that fight to destroy good and truth, toiled and produced those outflows.

There were a full process of such streams, like a principal current of flowing intelligence, entering the craving of each ruling evil; yet they could not be gathered into a single satisfied reception and brought to rest, because as each influx descended into their inmost appropriation it tormented them by the very ardor of their own love and the heat of their own desire. Those ruling evils were like self-renewing persuasions that do not come to an end; they were not exhausted, and continual descent of falsified influence maintained them through the whole span of their existing states.

This is the measure of the conflict, since it has brought into view the destructive affections and their gigantic strength. Notice that they are entangled, held in constraint, and fixed in every region of their domain. They are kept from open manifestation and are not presented to the perception of everyone who lives in the natural degree under the rule of spiritual death. Yet in their own order they are made manifest. The whole arrangement of merely natural life, separated from what is living, will be brought to an end and dissolved; all such appearances pass away. These evils will perish by the outburst of their own fury, which is more devastating than any external shock.

What can be grasped in a small outward perception is scarcely anything when set against the immeasurable abundance of the falsities that arise when truth is seized and inverted. For what is known outwardly is only a single current out of innumerable currents of thinking from general knowledges, drawn from inner arcana that are not disclosed to the natural mind.

Attend and be astonished at the degree of truth even in its lowest form, and how much it can be turned when it is made a covering for evil. Wonder at the magnitude of that divine humanity who carried such a burden. Grasp how great is the Divine, active in power: that which the evils could not withstand was greater than the measure of the good that entered into the outermost combat and bore an external covering of such scope, and thus how much was accomplished.

fills.notes: The clause points back to an earlier, already-given exposition; the oldest-layer register prefers simple anaphora rather than rhetorical embellishment.
The sense requires a brief anaphoric closure: they consumed the waters “as I told you about it,” i.e., about this mode of devouring and perverting. Keeps the impersonal instructional tone.
Outflow sequence: from the garment of waters → many waters pour out → from these derive the rivers. The substrate logic is derivation by emanated effects.
Fits the correspondential role of “mouth” as receptacle: the rulers’ craving receives the poured-out waters before further production.
Correspondentially the craving of evil is insatiable; the mouth is “not filled” by these influxes. This also prepares ¶7 where they cannot be satisfied to a single stomach.
The list-like construction suggests an added collective term: “those …, the warriors …, and all … laboured.” Marks the totality of destructive agencies producing the outflows.
Spiritual sense: the streams cannot be brought together into one satisfied reception. “Be gathered” supplies the needed process-term without importing later moralizing language.
They are compared to “images” of something—i.e., self-renewing persuasions/phantasms. “Images” fits the substrate’s cosmological descriptive register better than later ecclesial terms.
Opposite-sense correspondence: the rulers are like images of deception, i.e., persuasive falsities that replicate. Keeps the teaching impersonal and structural.
Pairs naturally with “rain” as continual downward influence sustaining their “existent days,” matching the spiritual explanation of continual descent of falsified influx.
The paragraph begins with a demonstrative summarizing what precedes: “This is how great a struggle …”.
The struggle “has revealed” the creatures/giants, matching the spiritual translation: “brought into view.”
Triplet requires a third constraint-term after “entwined, bound,”; “fixed” matches the spiritual sense of being held in a set state in every region.

fills.fill: but they are in their place
fills.notes: Bridges the concealment from common perception with the fact that they are manifest in their own order: hidden from general sight, yet ‘in their place’ they appear.
Required to complete the predication: “These rulers … revealed.” The oldest layer states the alternation: concealed to some, revealed in their own domain.
Applies the consummation motif in cosmological (not pastoral) terms: the universe of flesh dissolves “in that day,” i.e., at the appointed state of dissolution.
Completes the cadence “all pass away …,” corresponding to the spiritual sense that such appearances vanish swiftly when their supporting state ends.
Directly matches the correspondential point: a small outward stream counts “as nothing” compared with the vastness of the hidden waters.
Object of “See”: the didactic imperative points to the very subject under discussion—the measure of the waters as lowest truth covering.
Syntax requires a comparative: “the one whom these waters are greater than …”. Also fits the spiritual sense: what the evils could not withstand was greater in measure.

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the correspondential sequence: garment of waters (outer truth) → devoured by rulers (perverted) → outflow of many waters (derivative falsities) → rivers (streams of reasoning) → insatiable mouth and stomach (craving) → concealment from ‘every flesh’ yet manifestation in their own domain → dissolution of the universe of flesh. The least secure restorations are where the underlying manuscript likely carried a concrete simile (“like the images of …”) and a collective subject (“and all …”), which the spiritual logic narrows in function (self-renewing persuasions; totality of destructive agents) but not in exact wording.
